scenario: Build mkSet(smallRanges + mk(1000,4000,{pos:1000}) + mk(2000,3000,{pos:2000}) sorted by from with cmp).
expected: size 5002; set.chunk.length > 1; set.nextLayer.size truthy (non-zero); checkSet passes (between over [0, length] reports 5002 ranges, each at its pos).

port_notes: Helpers (mirrors/cm6/state/test/test-rangeset.ts:4-59). `Value` (:4-26) extends RangeValue: startSide = spec.startSide ?? 1; endSide = spec.endSide ?? spec.startSide ?? (empty ? 1 : -1); point = empty || !!spec.point; name = spec.name || null; pos = spec.pos ?? null; eq(other) = other instanceof Value && other.name == this.name (no identity shortcut in eq itself; cmpVal adds it). `Value.names(v)` joins, with '/', name or 'POINT' for every value that has a name or is a point (unnamed marks are skipped). `mk(from, to?, spec?)` (:30-34): if `to` is not a number it is the spec and to = from; a string spec means {name: spec}; the value is new Value(spec, from == to) (so an empty range is a point with sides 1/1, a non-empty one a mark with sides 1/-1 unless overridden) and the result is value.range(from, to); every mk call creates a new value object. `mkSet(ranges)` = RangeSet.of(ranges) without sort (:35). `cmp(a, b)` = a.from - b.from, used with Array.prototype.sort (stable) to sort range arrays (:28). `smallRanges` (:46-48): 5000 ranges mk(i, i + 1 + (i % 4), {pos: i}) for i in 0..4999, built once at module load; `set0()` (:49-50) builds mkSet(smallRanges) lazily once and returns the same set object afterwards. `checkSet(set)` (:52-59): set.between(0, set.length, ...) counting calls and asserting from == value.pos when pos is set, then asserting the count equals set.size; `set.length` is @internal (Q5).
